what_happened: The the person running Athena lifted the scope pause on the disk-fix line by hand. The line's second attempt had been rejected only because the verdict logic did not count GitHub's reused CI result as a test run. The verifier had passed the work. That verdict gap was fixed separately. The pause came from the scope guard reading the rejection as a sign the work had gone off course, so the the person running Athena overrode it.
cause: The verdict's evidence rule only recognised check results run by Athena itself. A change to where check results come from, here a reused CI result, was never traced through the rules that consume those records. The scope guard then treated the resulting rejection as spend with no progress and paused the line. It has no way to tell a system-caused rejection from a failure of the work, so only the the person running Athena could lift the pause.
prevention: Add a code check with two parts. First, any change to the source of check results must pass a test showing that the verdict and evidence rules accept the new source: replay a job whose tests were reused from CI and require the verdict to count them. Second, the scope guard must not count a rejection toward a pause when the verifier passed every criterion and the rejection came only from the evidence rule. In that case it should hold the line for automatic re-verification rather than pause it.
proposed_request: Make the scope guard separate system-caused rejections from work-caused ones. When a job is rejected only because the verdict's evidence rule did not accept a valid check source, such as a reused CI result, while the verifier passed every acceptance criterion, do not count that attempt's spend toward a line pause. Re-run the verdict automatically instead. Add a test that replays a job whose tests were reused from CI. It must show that the verdict counts the CI result as a test run, that the line is not paused, and that a rejection with an unmet criterion still counts toward a pause as before.
